claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my one child. His name is Alex and he's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he is still in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or NVQs up to Level 3) or approved training (such as a traineeship in England)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in full-time education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and studying for A-levels at sixth form college, he may still qualify.

**Did Alex start or enrol on his current course of A-levels before he turned 18?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he started his A-levels before he turned 18.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more question:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and upbringing (such as providing food, clothing, and looking after his welfare)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for Alex's day-to-day care. I provide everything he needs - food, clothing, and look after his welfare.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 18 years old
- He is in full-time non-advanced education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- He started his A-levels before turning 18
- He lives with you
- You are responsible for his day-to-day care

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Age & Education**: Although Alex is 18 (above the standard age of 16), Child Benefit can continue until a child turns 20 as long as they remain in approved education or training. A-levels at sixth form college count as approved non-advanced education.

✅ **Course Start Date**: Alex started his A-levels before he turned 18, which is an important requirement for continued eligibility.

✅ **Living Arrangements**: Alex lives with you.

✅ **Responsibility**: You are responsible for his day-to-day care, providing food, clothing, and looking after his welfare.

You should be able to continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex while he remains in approved full-time education, up until he turns 20.

If you haven't already, you can apply for Child Benefit or, if you're already receiving it, ensure you've notified HMRC that Alex is continuing in education so payments continue.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?
